review.assessment: This change introduces a brand-new src/lib.rs implementing a basic word counter that only splits on literal spaces and treats strings as case-sensitive. It passes the existing acceptance test by coincidence but completely omits the required case-insensitive normalization, robust non-alphanumeric splitting, and deterministic sorting logic. As a result, the implementation fails to satisfy any of the three core specifications in the task description.

findings.at: Defect 1: Case sensitivity ignored. The function does not normalize word casing before counting, so 'Apple' and 'apple' are stored as distinct entries.

findings.actual: "hello," and "world" treated as separate tokens with punctuation attached
findings.at: Defect 2: Fails to split on non-alphanumeric characters. The implementation uses .split(' '), which leaves punctuation, tabs, and newlines attached to words.
findings.defect: Fails to split on non-alphanumeric characters
findings.expected: "hello" and "world" counted separately with punctuation stripped

findings.at: Defect 3: Unsorted output. The function collects the HashMap iterator directly without sorting, resulting in arbitrary ordering.
